All levels (Bachelor, Master’s, and PhD) of inbound exchange students are eligible. 
Lecturers in Engineering, Business or Architecture related areas are welcome for teaching mobility at HCMUT. 
Non-academic staff (esp. from International Office) from partner universaities are welcome for one week mobility. 
One credit is equivalent to 50 hours of standardized learning time for the learner, including the time for scheduled 
lectures, guided instruction, self-study, research, experiential learning, and assessments/exams. 
For classroom teaching activities, one credit requires a minimum of 15 hours of lectures or 30 hours of practical 
work, experiments, discussions, in which one classroom hour is counted as 50 minutes. 
The teaching activities are organized between 06:00 and before 22:00 (periods 1 to 16) on all days of the week from 
Monday to Sunday. The scheduling of other learning activities related to the training program will be based on specific 
situations or particular academic levels. 
Classes are generally conducted face-to-face. 
Online learning is oraganized depending on specific situations in accordance with the academic regulations. 
All lecturers are required to use “Bach Khoa e-learning – BkeL” (an internal online platform at HCMUT) to facilitate 
their teaching activities and share course-related materials/documents to students.

Students who stay at HCMUT for academic exchange period are required to obtain a study visa before entering 
Vietnam, following the procedures below. 
1. After finalizing and signing a Learning Agreement, HCMUT sends students a visa request form to fill in. 
2. HCMUT submits all documents of the students’ study period to the Vietnamese Immigration Department 
for issuing the Visa Approval Letter. 
3. HCMUT sends the scanned Visa Approval Letter + Acceptance Letter to the students. 
4. The incoming students bring their original passports and the provided Visa Letter to the expected Vietnamese 
Embassy/Consulate in their home country to collect the visa. 
Notes:  
- The Visa Approval Letter issued by the Immigration Department will enable the students to obtain a visa shortly. 
- The incoming students had better NOT apply for a tourist visa before receiving the Visa Approval Letter. A tourist visa 
doesn’t mean for study purposes and will not be accepted for an exchange stay at HCMUT.  
 
 
 
The students need to submit a Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) application to our university with other required 
documents. We will submit the completed CoE application to the immigration office in Kyoto. As soon as we 
receive the CoE from the immigration office, we will send it to the student or the international office of your 
university by post. When the students receive the CoE, please have them apply immediately for a visa at the 
nearest Japanese embassy/consulate in your country. 
Before students leave their countries, we strongly recommend that they obtain travel insurance, which covers 
difficulties, medical helps or incidents during travel from and back to their countries. 
The students are required to provide a copy of their insurance to HCMUT one week before their arrival. 
Imcoming students from HCMUT’s partners with valid agreements can benefit from tuition waivers. 
Exchange students can have the opportunity to receive scholarship s to partly cover necessary expenses 
during their mobility period. 
We may decline to accept students according to our capacity, the changes in the circumstances due to infectious 
disease prevalence or natural disasters. 
Regarding COVID-19, students must follow the Vietnamese government / HCMUTguidelines. Please note that HCMUT 
may refuse to accept students if future immigration restrictions are imposed by the Vietnamese government.
